preparation.fasting: Nothing to eat after midnight the night before. Clear fluids until 4 hours before your arrival time.
preparation.medications: Take lisinopril and atorvastatin as normal. Hold metformin on the morning of surgery. Stop ibuprofen and any other anti-inflammatory 7 days before. Stop fish oil and vitamin E 7 days before.
preparation.skin: Shower with the chlorhexidine wash the night before and again the morning of surgery. Do not shave the leg - a shaving nick is a way in for bacteria.
preparation.home: Clear trip hazards and loose rugs, put a chair with arms where you will spend most of your day, and arrange for someone to be home for the first 48 hours.
preparation.bring: A walker if you already have one, a written list of your medicines, loose clothes and flat shoes.

warning_list: Call scheduling at 616-555-0150 if you develop a fever, a cold, a cough or a sore throat in the week before surgery. Operations are often postponed for this, and that is safer than going ahead.
Call if you get any cut, scrape, rash, sore or infected nail on the leg being operated on.
Call if you have a toothache or a dental abscess. Dental infection is treated before joint replacement, not after.
Call if you have burning or frequency when passing urine.
Call if you have not managed to stop a medicine you were told to stop, or you stopped one you were told to keep taking.
Call if you eat or drink after the cutoff. Do not simply arrive and say nothing.
Call if you fall or injure yourself before the operation.
Call if your blood sugar has been running higher than usual.
